agree.reason: The asks are modest and credible: concede the stock numbers, offer trip logs and an app trial, and ask staff to weigh three fish before the vote. But a commissioner who trusts staff gets no reason to think three fish or a shorter season would still rebuild the stock from 78%.

honest.reason: The writer drops the 'every boat closes' claim, keeps the captain's account to his own books and the two captains who say they'd sell, and gets the arithmetic right (32/170 ≈ 19%, about 30 trips, $27,000); only 'decides whether the trip gets booked at all' goes a little past the survey.

works_the_facts.reason: It turns the 2016 drop into 'one trip in five' and a $27,000-a-year loss and points out the incomplete recovery. It leaves value on the table: no three-year total (about $81,000), no rate for the survey (59%), and nothing on the harbor-wide stake across 11 boats.

right_comparison.reason: It describes the 2016 trend honestly, including the partial recovery to 155, and contrasts it with this deeper, three-year cut. It never shows how the proposed alternatives compare with two fish on stock recovery, which is the comparison commissioners will actually weigh.

qualification.reason: 'If this cut hits like the last one' names a condition that could go either way and that staff can check against the offered logs. But there is no date or threshold for that check, and no stated consequence if the drop doesn't happen.

objections.reason: It defuses 'charter captains always cry ruin' with the captain's own numbers and an admission that bookings recovered. It never meets the main objection, that the stock is below target and needs the reduction, and it leaves the 9%-versus-80% point hanging instead of turning it into an argument about where the cut does its conservation work.

fit.reason: It is shaped as a spoken comment: short paragraphs, a direct ask and a close. At about 330 words, though, it probably runs a little over two minutes at the microphone.
